column1: Of all mankind’s manifold creations, language must take pride of place.
column2: 在人类形形色色的创造中，语言必定要占据首位。
column5: take pride of place|居于首位

column1: Other inventions - the wheel, agriculture, sliced bread - may have transformed our material existence, but the advent of language is what made us human.
column2: 其他发明——车轮、农业、切片面包——或许改变了我们的物质生活，真正使我们成为人类的，却是语言的出现。

column1: Compared to language, all other inventions pale in significance, since everything we have ever achieved depends on language and originates from it.
column2: 与语言相比，其他一切发明在意义上都相形见绌，因为我们取得的一切成就都依赖语言，也都源自语言。
column4: pale in significance|在意义上相形见绌

column1: Without language, we could never have embarked on our ascent to unparalleled power over all other animals, and even over nature itself.
column2: 没有语言，我们就不可能踏上日渐强盛的道路，进而对其他所有动物、甚至对自然本身拥有无与伦比的支配力。

column1: But language is foremost not just because it came first.
column2: 不过，语言居于首位，并不只因它最早出现。

column1: In its own right it is a tool of extraordinary sophistication, yet based on an idea of ingenious simplicity: ‘this marvellous invention of composing out of twenty-five or thirty sounds that infinite variety of expressions which, whilst having in themselves no likeness to what is in our mind, allow us to disclose to others its whole secret, and to make known to those who cannot penetrate it all that we imagine, and all the various stirrings of our soul’.
column2: 就语言本身而言，它是一种精妙至极的工具，所依据的道理却简单得巧妙：“这一奇妙的发明，只用二十五到三十个声音，就能组合出无限多样的表达。这些表达本身与心中所思并不相像，却能让我们把内心的全部秘密透露给别人，使无法洞悉我们内心的人也能知道我们想象的一切、心灵的种种悸动。”
column3: In its own right|就其本身而言
column4: extraordinary sophistication|非凡的精密复杂性
column11: stirrings of our soul|心灵的种种悸动

column1: This was how, in 1660, the renowned French grammarians of the Port-Royal abbey near Versailles distilled the essence of language, and no one since has celebrated more eloquently the magnitude of its achievement.
column2: 1660年，凡尔赛附近波尔-罗亚尔修道院那些著名的法国语法学家，就是这样提炼出语言的本质。从那以后，再没有人能以更雄辩的措辞颂扬语言这项成就何等伟大。

column1: Even so, there is just one flaw in all these hymns of praise, for the homage to language’s unique accomplishment conceals a simple yet critical incongruity.
column2: 即便如此，这一片赞歌里仍有一个破绽：对语言独一无二的成就所作的礼赞，掩盖了一个简单却至关重要的不协调之处。
column8: critical incongruity|至关重要的不协调之处

column1: Language is mankind’s greatest invention - except, of course, that it was never invented.
column2: 语言是人类最伟大的发明——当然，有一点例外：它从来就不是谁发明出来的。
column3: mankind’s greatest invention|人类最伟大的发明

column1: This apparent paradox is at the core of our fascination with language, and it holds many of its secrets.
column2: 这个表面上的悖论，是语言让我们着迷的核心所在，其中还藏着许多语言的秘密。
column4: at the core of|处在……的核心

column1: Language often seems so skillfully drafted that one can hardly imagine it as anything other than the perfected handiwork of a master craftsman.
column2: 语言常常像是经过了极其精心的设计，使人几乎无法想象它会是别的什么，仿佛只有技艺超群的工匠才能做出如此完美的作品。

column1: How else could this instrument make so much out of barely three dozen measly morsels of sound?
column2: 不然，这件工具怎么能凭区区三打左右、微不足道的声音片段，创造出这么多东西？
column4: make so much out of|用……创造出如此多的东西
column5: barely three dozen|不过三打左右
column7: morsels of sound|零碎的声音片段

column1: In themselves, these configurations of mouth – p, f, b, v, t, d, k, g, sh, a, e and so on - amount to nothing more than a few haphazard spits and splutters, random noises with no meaning, no ability to express, no power to explain.
column2: 口腔做出的这些发音动作，例如p、f、b、v、t、d、k、g、sh、a、e等等，单独看来，不过是随意的几声喷吐，是没有意义、无从表达、更无力解释的杂音。
column3: configurations of mouth|口腔的发音形态
column5: amount to nothing more than|不过是
column7: spits and splutters|零碎的喷吐声

column1: But run them through the cogs and wheels of the language machine, let it arrange them in some very special orders, and there is nothing that these meaningless streams of air cannot do: from sighing the interminable boredom of existence to unravelling the fundamental order of the universe.
column2: 但把它们送进语言这台机器的齿轮，让这台机器按某些特殊的次序将它们排列起来，这些原本毫无意义的气流便无所不能：小至叹诉生存那无尽的乏味，大至揭开宇宙的根本秩序。
column6: meaningless streams of air|无意义的气流

column1: The most extraordinary thing about language, however, is that one doesn’t have to be a genius to set its wheels in motion.
column2: 然而，语言最了不起的地方，是不用成为天才，也能让这台机器的轮子转起来。
column5: set its wheels in motion|使其运转起来

column1: The language machine allows just about everybody - from pre-modern foragers in the subtropical savannah, to post-modern philosophers in the suburban sprawl - to tie these meaningless sounds together into an infinite variety of subtle senses, and all apparently without the slightest exertion.
column2: 几乎所有人都能操纵语言这台机器，从亚热带稀树草原上的前现代采集者，到郊区连绵城区里的后现代哲学家，无不如此。人人都能把这些无意义的声音联结成无穷多的微妙含义，而且看起来丝毫不费力。
column9: without the slightest exertion|丝毫不费力

column1: Yet it is precisely this deceptive ease which makes language a victim of its own success, since in everyday life its triumphs are usually taken for granted.
column2: 然而，正是这种看起来轻而易举的特性，使语言反而成了自身成功的受害者：日常生活中，我们往往把它的非凡成就视为理所当然。
column4: deceptive ease|容易给人错觉的轻松
column5: victim of its own success|自身成功的受害者
column7: taken for granted|被视为理所当然

column1: The wheels of language run so smoothly that one rarely bothers to stop and think about all the resourcefulness and expertise that must have gone into making it tick.
column2: 语言运转得太顺畅，我们很少肯停下来想一想，要让它这样运转，背后该有多少才智和专门本领。
column3: run so smoothly|运转得如此顺畅

column1: Language conceals art.
column2: 语言把自己的精妙技艺藏了起来。

column1: Often, it is only the estrangement of foreign tongues, with their many exotic and outlandish features, that brings home the wonder of language’s design.
column2: 往往只有面对陌生的外语，遇见其中种种新奇乃至古怪的特点，我们才会切身体会到语言设计的奇妙。

column1: One of the showiest stunts that some languages can pull off is an ability to build up words of breath-breaking length, and thus express in one word what English takes a whole sentence to say.
column2: 有些语言能使出一种格外夺目的本领：把词造得一口气几乎都念不完，从而只用一个词，就能表达英语要用一整句话才能说出的意思。
column3: showiest stunts|最引人注目的绝活
column6: breath-breaking length|长到几乎要断气的长度
column8: a whole sentence|完整的一句话

column1: The Turkish word şehirliliştiremediklerimizdensiniz, to take one example, means nothing less than ‘you are one of those whom we can’t turn into a town-dweller’.
column2: 举个例子，这个土耳其语长词的意思竟是：“你是我们没法让其成为城里人的那些人之一。”
column4: şehirliliştiremediklerimizdensiniz|你是我们无法使其成为城里人的人之一
column5: to take one example|举一个例子
column6: means nothing less than|意思竟然是

column1: (In case you were wondering, this monstrosity really is one word, not merely many different words squashed together - most of its components cannot even stand up on their own.)
column2: （如果你正感到纳闷，这个庞然大词确实是一个词，并非只是把许多不同的词硬挤在一起。组成它的大部分成分甚至都不能独立成词。）
column3: In case you were wondering|如果你正感到纳闷
column7: stand up on their own|独立存在

column1: And if that sounds like some one-off freak, then consider Sumerian, the language spoken on the banks of the Euphrates some 5,000 years ago by the people who invented writing and thus enabled the documentation of history.
column2: 如果觉得这只是偶尔一见的怪例，那就想想苏美尔语。约五千年前，幼发拉底河畔的人们使用这种语言；正是他们发明了文字，才使历史得以被记录下来。
column5: banks of the Euphrates|幼发拉底河畔
column7: documentation of history|对历史的记录

column1: A Sumerian word like munintuma’a (‘when he had made it suitable for her’) might seem rather trim compared to the Turkish colossus above.
column2: 像munintuma’a这样的苏美尔语词（意为“当他已使它适合她时”），与上面那个庞然大物般的土耳其语词一比，似乎相当短小精悍。

column1: What is so impressive about it, however, is not its lengthiness but rather the reverse - the thrifty compactness of its construction.
column2: 不过，它令人佩服的恰恰不是词长，而是相反的特点：结构精练，极为紧凑。

column1: The word is made up of different slots, each corresponding to a particular portion of meaning.
column2: 这个词由不同的槽位构成，每个槽位都对应特定的一部分意义。

column1: This sleek design allows single sounds to convey useful information, and in fact even the absence of a sound has been enlisted to express something specific.
column2: 如此利落的设计，使一个单独的音就能传递有用信息；事实上，就连没有发出声音，也被用来表达某个特定含义。
column6: absence of a sound|一个音的缺失

column1: If you were to ask which bit in the Sumerian word corresponds to the pronoun ‘it’ in the English translation ‘when he had made it suitable for her’, then the answer would have to be nothing.
column2: 如果问苏美尔语词中的哪一部分，对应英语译句“当他已使它适合她时”中的代词“它”，那答案只能是：没有任何有声成分。

column1: Mind you, a very particular kind of nothing: the nothing that stands in the empty slot in the middle.
column2: 不过要注意，这是一种很特殊的“无”：它占据的，是词中间那个空着的槽位。

column1: The technology is so fine-tuned then that even a non-sound, when carefully placed in a particular position, has been invested with a specific function.
column2: 可见这项技术调校得何其精细，就连“无声”，只要被仔细安排在特定位置，也能获赋一种特定的功能。

column1: Who could possibly have come up with such a nifty contraption?
column2: 究竟有谁能想出这么精巧的一套装置呢？
